issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Stock class (with specific methods like add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock) and instruct SealSaloon to hold a static final Stock stock. However, the template repository provides an Inventory class implementing the stock functionality while src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java is empty. The solution repository also uses Inventory (SealSaloon declares a static final Inventory stock). This inconsistency in the expected type/name (Stock vs Inventory) will confuse students about which class to use and can lead to compilation or design mismatches when they implement SealSaloon according to the problem text.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming and types consistent across problem statement, template, and solution. Either (A) update the template to provide a working Stock class (move/rename Inventory.java to Stock.java and remove or populate the empty Stock.java) and adjust references in problem text to Stock; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to use Inventory instead of Stock so it matches the template and solution. Ensure SealSaloon and UML use the same class name and type for the shared stock.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' as the saloon's shared inventory, but the provided template and solution code use the name 'Inventory' for that same conceptual entity (and Stock.java is empty). This mismatch between 'Stock' (problem/UML) and 'Inventory' (code) can confuse students when mapping requirements to the template implementation and when implementing or locating the expected class.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Either rename the code-side Inventory class/file to Stock (and update references) to match the problem statement/UML, or update the problem statement/UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock'. Ensure Stock.java in the template is removed or contains the renamed class to avoid duplicate/empty files.
